cues.text: Simulated model, assumed signs. The proboscis reach is keyframed; the brain model gets sugar gustatory receptor neurons (sugar GRNs) as input — the taste cells for sweetness.
Simulated model: the sugar GRNs fire into the gnathal ganglia, the taste gateway wrapped around the esophagus.
Simulated model: the sweet taste signal climbs through the wedge and prow toward motor circuits.
Simulated model: MN9, a motor neuron that extends the proboscis, switches on — the sugar-GRN to MN9 path traced by Shiu et al. 2024.
Simulated model: the keyframed proboscis extends as simulated MN9 firing peaks — a plausible output, not a measured muscle drive.
Simulated model: taste activity lingers in the gnathal ganglia while the olfactory lobes stay quiet — no smell in this simulated meal.
Simulated model: the sugar drive ends and the simulated GRN firing decays back to baseline.

qa.q: What triggers feeding in the model?
qa.a: Sugar gustatory receptor neurons (sugar GRNs) — the input set used in the published example of Shiu et al. 2024.
A motor neuron that extends the proboscis. Shiu et al. 2024 showed simulated sugar-GRN input reaches MN9 through the connectome.
No — every spike is simulated by the Shiu et al. 2024 model, with partly assumed neurotransmitter signs.
It is keyframed by hand, not recorded; only the simulated brain activity comes from the model.
